 Ranveer Singh, Aman Gupta launch men's grooming brand H.I.M; enter Rs 2.2 lakh crore BPC market 
 Ranveer Singh and Aman Gupta have co-founded H.I.M, a new men's personal care brand in India. The product line includes eight items focused on skincare and haircare suited for Indian men's needs. This initiative aims to tap into the growing men's grooming market, which is currently underrepresented. H.I.M's products utilize innovative ingredients developed for efficacy under Indian conditions. E ETRetail Desk

 Actor Ranveer Singh and boAt co-founder Aman Gupta have launched H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man), a men's personal care brand targeting India's growing grooming market with an eight-product range spanning face, body and hair care. Co-founded by the duo, H.I.M is positioned around formulations developed specifically for Indian male skin, climate and biology. The range is powered by IN·XT™, a proprietary molecule developed exclusively for the brand, and is priced between Rs 299 and Rs 899. The launch comes amid growth in India's beauty and personal care (BPC) market, estimated at approximately Rs 2.2 lakh crore and projected to nearly double to Rs 4 lakh crore by FY31, according to the company's announcement. Despite the market's scale, men account for less than 10 per cent of India's beauty and personal care spending, highlighting the opportunity the founders are looking to tap through a dedicated men's personal care proposition. H.I.M's initial portfolio comprises face wash, face cream, sunscreen, body wash, body lotion, shampoo, hair serum and an exfoliating soap bar. The products incorporate ingredients such as salicylic acid, niacinamide, ceramides, hyaluronic acid, Redensyl and AnaGain, targeting concerns including oily skin, body acne, sun protection, dandruff and hair health. The brand's proprietary IN·XT™ technology is designed to support the delivery of active skincare ingredients into the skin. According to the company, its formulations draw on research involving Indian male skin and testing under conditions of Indian heat, humidity and pollution. "Someone once told me I was 'too handsome for an Indian.' Being Indian should never make being handsome a surprise. I've always taken pride in looking after myself, but I started to realise my products were never really made for me, or for our skin, our weather and our water. Aman and I worked with scientists to understand Indian male skin and develop H.I.M. I tested every formulation, from the first samples to the final products," said Ranveer Singh, Co-founder, H.I.M. Gupta said the opportunity is being driven by changing consumer awareness and growing interest in men's skincare. "India's beauty and personal care market is Rs 2.2 lakh crore today and is projected to nearly double to Rs 4 lakh crore by FY2031. Even searches for men's skincare routines are up 850 per cent over the last five years. Indian men are finally talking about their skin, reading labels and building routines," said Aman Gupta, Co-founder, H.I.M. He added that Singh was closely involved in product development, testing and the formulation process. The brand is launching through its own website, Amazon and quick-commerce platform Blinkit, giving it access to both online shoppers and consumers seeking faster delivery of personal care products. H.I.M is being built under OFF/BEAT Studios, the venture studio founded by Gupta, which focuses on developing consumer brands across high-growth categories. Comments
